name: Viana do Castelo – Cabedelo
notes: Windiest spot in Portugal (nortada): waves outside, flatter by the river-mouth pier. Also: Caminha – Moledo (waves).

name: Esposende – Ofir
notes: Flat knee-deep lagoon in the Cávado estuary behind the Ofir sandspit (walk or school boat), waves on the sea side.

name: Murtosa – Ria de Aveiro
notes: Flat shallow lagoon, nortada thermal Apr–Oct; school (Clube Nortada). Also: Aveiro – Praia da Barra (waves on the ocean side).

name: Lagoa de Óbidos
notes: Flat, waist-deep lagoon; lighter wind (big kites). Guides report kiting closed in summer (about 15 Jun–15 Sep) near the mouth and in the north of the lagoon: then ride by the sailing school or at Bom Sucesso. Also: Peniche – Baleal (ocean).

name: Guincho
notes: Very strong nortada, waves, rocks in the middle of the bay: advanced riders.

name: Fonte da Telha
notes: Closest spot to Lisbon; all levels, lighter wind; very busy in summer. Also: São João da Caparica (same coast, further north).

name: Alcochete
notes: Flat, shallow water on the Tagus estuary across from Lisbon (Praia dos Moinhos); beginner friendly, school on site. Stones; mud flats at low tide; water quality varies.

name: Lagoa de Albufeira
notes: Flat-water lagoon behind the sandbar; too shallow at low tide and in dry summers, deeper on the east side.

name: Lagos – Meia Praia
notes: Long sandy bay with schools on the beach; waves can build.

name: Alvor
notes: Ria de Alvor: flat, mostly waist-deep lagoon; launch on the sandspit by the dunes (dirt track from Alvor village). NW thermal, gusty near the edges; water from mid tide, some current.

name: Praia de Faro
notes: Ilha de Faro: waves on the ocean, flat water in the Ria Formosa (tide matters). The Faro maritime authority has restricted kiting in the Ria Formosa before: check local rules. Also: Fuseta, Cabanas de Tavira.

name: Manta Rota
notes: Long sandy beach in the east Algarve: SW thermal or E Levante, mostly flat to small waves; school (AlturaKites). Also: Cacela Velha.

name: Porto Santo
notes: 9 km beach; N wind is side-offshore and gusty in summer: experienced riders.
